verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/sec_filings_provider.py:368-372 keeps only text values of the sections dict. sec-edgar-mcp 1.0.8 get_filing_sections returns only {has_financials: true} for a 10-Q and {} for any other non-10-K form, so zero sections come out. The docstring at :363-364 treats that as 'a real empty' on the false premise that the upstream sections 10-Qs. get_filing :653-661 then caches the zero-section FilingDetail for 24h. FilingViewer.tsx:193 shows 'No section selected.' with no reason, and sec_tools.py:101-113 returns ok:true with an empty filing.
verdicts.fix_shape: In get_filing, when _sections_from_payload yields no text sections, call the upstream get_filing_content tool (same sec-edgar-mcp; it returns the filing text capped at 50,000 chars) and wrap the text in the existing single 'Filing Content' section (the bare-text branch at :381-391). If that also yields no text, raise an uncached ProviderError with a stated reason, so the panel shows its error state and sec_filing_content returns ok:false. Correct the docstring at :363-364.

verdicts.failure_sources: R15-DATA-038: baseline 0 (no 'certification failures so far' clause in its register note; not in any stage-c/batch-*/VERDICTS.json not_certified list; no partial or regression verdict in REFUTATION_AUDIT.json or round-*/REFUTATION_AUDIT.json), plus 1 for this partial
verdicts.note: Reproduces at HEAD on my own sidecar :52420 and my own sec-edgar-mcp :52421. AAPL 10-Q 0000320193-23-000077: form 10-Q, date 2023-08-04, 0 sections, total_chars 0. AAPL 8-K: also 0. AAPL 10-K: business and risk_factors, 20,000 chars. The raw upstream 10-Q payload is sections {has_financials:true}, and the agent tool returns ok:true with 0 sections. The verdict lands on R15-DATA-038, not the shard's tie. DATA-038 (fixed, silent-parse-drop) has fix_shape 'treat a success payload that parses to zero rows as a logged parse error, not a cacheable empty'. Its stated 10-K repro holds, but the 10-Q and 8-K success payloads still parse to zero rows and are cached 24h. R15-DATA-007 (the shard's tie) is not it: metadata is real now. R15-LEAD-010 (the tie of the same finding rc1-vshard-7:4, covered by this verdict) is not it either: the lookup succeeds. R15-CODE-DATA-013 folded the batch-12 aside '/sections returns [] for 10-Q' on the claim that deleting the dead route resolves it. That is wrong, because get_filing, the viewer's main route and sec_filing_content all return 0 sections. Severity raised from medium to high: every non-10-K filing opens blank and the agent is told ok with empty content.

verdicts.note: The class reproduces, but not on the shard's evidence. All 20 AMAL items come from AMAL's own Yahoo per-symbol feed (source 'Yahoo! Finance: AMAL News'; region-feed items are dropped untagged by news_provider.enrich), and they are on-entity. The 'Broadcom upgraded, Ultragenyx downgraded' roundup contains an Amalgamated Financial call, and 'CFO Sells ... Regional Bank' is the Form-4 story on Amalgamated CFO Jason Darby. row_relevant=false there is a title-only false negative. The real repro is a US ticker that is a common word. For IT (Gartner) the in-process DEEP researcher received 28 news items, 8 of them MarketWatch/Insider Monkey region headlines tagged via the word 'it' (Palantir, Securitize, Interparfums), all 8 in the extraction prompt, gate note None. Rated high rather than critical: off-entity evidence is shown reaching extraction and cited sources, but no published-brief misattribution was demonstrated (that needs an LLM run; hosted lanes are out of bounds). The over-tagging itself is rc1-vshard-1:2 (DATA-030).

verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/news_provider.py:583 keeps every bare or suffixed ticker of 2+ characters as a text alias, and :606-607 matches aliases case-insensitively with \b..\b over title and summary. A bare ticker that is the leading word of another listed company's name (RELIANCE and 'Reliance Power', LT and 'LT Foods', ITC and 'ITC Hotels') or an English word (IT, ON, ALL) therefore tags unrelated headlines.
verdicts.fix_shape: In news_provider._aliases and _tag_symbols, match ticker aliases (bare and suffixed) case-sensitively as uppercase tokens and keep only the company-name alias case-insensitive. Drop the bare-ticker text alias when the ticker is the first word of a different listed company's name in the resolver masters (RELIANCE: Reliance Power and Reliance Infrastructure; LT: LT Foods; ITC: ITC Hotels), leaving the company-name alias and per-symbol-feed provenance to tag those symbols.

verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/search/mojeek.py:114-128 treats only 403 and 429 as a block, so a 200 challenge page is parsed (:123) to zero rows and returned as a successful empty response. sidecar/services/search/keyless.py:196-206: _filter_results([]) gives blocked=0, so the 'blocked and not results' branch never fires, breaker.record_success() (:205) resets the failure count and any_engine_answered=True (:206). :227-230 then return a healthy empty SearchResponse instead of the typed rate_limited error. INTERSTITIAL_MARKERS (:79-84) are checked only on parsed rows, never on a page that parsed to zero rows.
verdicts.fix_shape: In MojeekSearchBackend.search, when _parse returns no rows on a 200, check the raw page text for challenge markers (the keyless INTERSTITIAL_MARKERS plus page-level 'captcha' and 'complete this challenge'). If one is present, raise SearchError('Mojeek: blocked (challenge page)', reason=SEARCH_REASON_RATE_LIMITED). The keyless loop then counts the failure against the breaker, keeps any_engine_answered false, and raises the typed rate_limited error when every engine is blocked.

verdicts.note: Live at HEAD. A direct Mojeek probe returns HTTP 200, 5519 bytes: 'Captcha ... JavaScript is required to complete this challenge.' The real MojeekSearchBackend inside KeylessSearchBackend returned 'OK results 0 backend keyless', and the mojeek breaker went from 1 failure to 0. The full web_search tool then returned ok:true, backend keyless-fallback, 0 results, no note, while at the same moment DDG was unreachable, Brave 429 and Mojeek on the captcha, i.e. all blocked. RESEARCH-022 (fixed, keyless-breaker-accounting) has a fix_shape that explicitly includes '(or a 200 parses to zero rows with block markers)'. That clause was never implemented, while its stated row-level stub repro holds (pytest test_keyless_backend.py -k 'challenge or block or interstitial': 3 passed). The residual reproduces every symptom in the entry's title. R15-CODE-AGENT-008 (layer-leak) is not the class.

verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/screener.py:555 (_fetch_pair: provider_registry.get_fundamentals(symbol) with no region), :574 (get_quote(symbol, asset_class) with no region) and :1078 (_enrich_survivors: get_fundamentals(key) with no region). provider_registry._effective_region (provider_registry.py:312-326) defers a ticker that is in both masters to the session region, so in an IN session a bare S&P 500 ticker resolves to the NSE company. _store_pair (:585-591) and upsert_info(key, rich) (:1094) then write it, stamped live, under the bare universe key, and every later session, US included, serves it.
verdicts.fix_shape: Thread the universe's intrinsic region into the per-symbol fetches: sp500 maps to 'US'; the India universes and nifty50 map to 'IN'; custom keeps None and defers to the locale. Pass it through _fetch_pair and _enrich_survivors into provider_registry.get_fundamentals(symbol, region=...) and get_quote(symbol, asset_class, region). As a guard, have _store_pair and upsert_info refuse and log a result whose resolved listing differs from the key (a Fundamentals.symbol of 'PTC.NS' under key 'PTC'), so an already-poisoned row is never refreshed with the wrong entity.

Assert the recorded region is 'US', the HAL row is 'Halliburton Company'/USD, and the coverage has no 'INR'. Add the same assertion for the _enrich_survivors path. Live, on a fresh data dir: curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Vysted-Region: IN' -d '{"universe":"sp500","criteria":[],"limit":600}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/screener/run | jq '[.rows[]|select(.currency=="INR")]|length' prints 0.
verdicts.note: Live at HEAD on a fresh scratch store. One IN-session sp500 screen served HAL as Hindustan Aeronautics (INR 4800, live), CCL as CCL Products (India), IEX as Indian Energy Exchange and ACGL as Automobile Corporation of Goa, with coverage 'spans INR, USD'. The store then held those Indian rows under the bare S&P 500 keys, and an immediate US-session sp500 screen served the same four Indian rows. /fundamentals/PTC resolves to PTC.NS under IN and to PTC Inc. under US. Not LEAD-013 (stale-static-reference-data): the sp500 pack is correct, and the seed packs key IN rows with a suffix. Related to R15-DATA-002 (blocked_tier4, wrong-entity-ticker-collision), but its fix carries the frontend's picked /resolve candidate through panel fan-out and cannot reach screener._fetch_pair or _enrich_survivors, where the universe itself carries the region. The cross-session store poisoning is not in DATA-002 either. Severity raised from medium to high: a core flow (the S&P 500 screen and the agent screener tool) serves non-members as live rows and drops real members, persistently. Not critical, because each wrong row shows its own Indian name and INR, so the swap is visible.
